summary: Iteration 5 backend-only test of SMS OTP fallback + phone_number identifier support. Wrote 19 pytest cases across 6 test classes (TestMemberPhone, TestInvitePhone, TestAuthMe, TestForgotSMS, TestEmailRegression, TestUniqueIndex). 18/19 passed. Verified: (1) POST/PUT /members phone normalization + duplicate 409 + partial-unique index enforcement; (2) POST /members/invite phone + duplicate 409; (3) PUT /auth/me updates name/phone/instrument/bio, returns user_public with phone_number, 409 on phone conflict; (4) POST /auth/forgot-password-sms with linked phone → {success:true, delivered:false, channel:'sms'} + password_reset_otps doc with channel='sms', otp_plain=6-digit, delivery_status='failed', phone_number=E.164; (5) member with no phone via email lookup → generic {success:true, delivered:false, message contains 'No phone number linked'} and NO OTP doc created; (6) unknown phone → {success:true, delivered:true} (no enumeration) and no DB entry; (7) GET /admin/pending-otps surfaces SMS entry with otp_plain + delivery_error but NO otp_hash; (8) verify-otp/reset-password accept {phone, otp}, wrong OTP 400, correct → 200, login with new password works, OTP marked used (reuse → 400); (9) Regressions all green: email forgot/verify/reset by email still works, admin1 email delivered=true, admin2 email delivered=false with plaintext exposed, admin login/me OK, brute-force lockout 429 after 5 fails.

minor.issue: normalize_phone('abc') returns None instead of raising 400. Any all-non-digit/non-plus string (e.g. 'abc', '---', 'hello') is silently stripped to empty and treated as 'no phone'. The E.164 regex check is never reached. Spec required: invalid non-E.164 phone like 'abc' must return 400. Fix: in normalize_phone, if the caller passed a non-empty raw string but the stripped value is empty, raise HTTPException(400, 'Phone must be E.164 (e.g. +14155552671)') instead of returning None.

action_items: Fix normalize_phone to raise 400 when the input is non-empty but strips to empty (garbage like 'abc'). Currently it silently returns None and the member is created with phone_number=null. All other invalid formats (e.g. '123', '+abc') already correctly 400.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now >1500 lines — long overdue to split into routers (auth, members, events, admin, sms/email).

otp_plain is persisted in Mongo when delivery fails (both channels). Add a TTL index on password_reset_otps.expires_at so plaintext OTPs auto-purge after 10 min. Currently expired-but-unused docs linger indefinitely (only filtered at read time in admin_pending_otps).

forgot_password_sms with unknown phone returns delivered:true (spec-compliant to avoid enumeration) but forgot_password with unknown email returns delivered:true as well only because `delivered` defaults to True and the `if user and email:` branch is skipped — this is fragile. Prefer an explicit constant response to make the anti-enumeration intent obvious.

normalize_phone treats input without '+' as already-country-coded and just prepends '+'. So a US 10-digit number '4155552671' becomes '+4155552671' (invalid country) rather than being rejected. Consider requiring '+' or documenting this behavior.

PUT /auth/me and PUT /members/{id} use model_dump(exclude_none=True), so passing phone_number: null in JSON is dropped before reaching the handler — the only way to clear a phone is to pass empty string, which normalize_phone converts to None. This is undocumented and inconsistent with the review request wording ('phone_number: null clears it'). Consider Optional[str] with a sentinel or a dedicated DELETE sub-route.

The single failing test (test_create_invalid_phone_returns_400) will pass once normalize_phone is fixed to raise 400 on empty-after-strip inputs. All other SMS + phone-identifier scenarios pass — no regressions introduced.
rca of the issue: normalize_phone(raw='abc') flow: v = re.sub(r'[^\d+]', '', 'abc') → '' → hits `if not v: return None` and returns None early. The E.164 regex validation on line 74 is bypassed. Consequence: create_member/update_member/invite/PUT auth/me all accept 'abc' as if no phone were provided, and store phone_number=null. Fix (1-line): distinguish between 'no phone provided' (raw is falsy) and 'phone provided but garbage' (raw truthy, stripped empty). Suggested patch: change the early-return block to `if not raw or not raw.strip(): return None` before doing the regex strip, then after `v = re.sub(...)` treat empty v as invalid (raise 400). Impact is low (garbage-in → null stored) but violates the API contract.
